title: Kernspan: a machine shop website told through one part
excerpt: A website study for a family CNC machine shop. One part, a truck cab damper, stays on screen for the whole homepage as a 3D model and takes itself apart as you scroll. The pages a buyer reads stay calm and static.
challenge: Most machine shop websites list machines and certificates, and they look alike. A buyer cannot see from a list how carefully a shop works. The study asks how a small shop can show that care on its own site, with one part and no film crew.
solution: The homepage follows one part from start to finish. The cab damper is built in code as a 3D model and sits behind the text for the whole page. Scrolling turns it, cuts it open, pulls its modules apart and puts it back together, while short blocks of copy cover manufacturing, products and the company. The subpages for manufacturing, products, company, careers and contact carry no 3D. They hold what a buyer checks: machine tables, certificates and contact details. The company name, the people and the legal details in this study are placeholders.
